chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who made the divorce of his wife in the hands of two men: so one of them divorced her and the other refused. So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) refused to validate that until both of them gather together in consensus upon the divorce.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a delegated divorce to be valid if two agents are appointed?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmits this ruling from Imam Ali (AS), establishing that in a delegated divorce (taliq) assigned to two agents, the act is not valid unless both concur, preventing unilateral action. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on joint authority and consensus in agency contracts, ensuring that the delegation is executed as a unified act rather than separate, potentially conflicting decisions. The ruling underscores the precision required in legal representation (wakalah) within family law.
